title: 8 Best No-Code Front-End Builders for Your Backend in 2026
summary: Eight no-code front-end builders that sit on top of a backend you already have, split by whether you are building for your team or your customers.
body_markdown:
If you already have a backend, whether Postgres, Supabase, Xano, Firebase or a REST API, you do not need an all-in-one platform that wants to own your data too. You need a front end that connects to what exists. The main split is who the front end is for: your own team, or your customers.


Below are eight no-code front-end builders, with the point where each one stops. For database-specific options, see the[best PostgreSQL frontend builders](https://www.jetadmin.io/blog/best-postgresql-frontend-builders/) .


## What a no-code front end for your backend needs


- Native connectors to your database or API, not just a built-in database.
- Reading and writing data, with validation.
- Authentication and per-user access to data.
- Room for custom code when the visual editor runs out.
- Hosting on your domain.


## The eight builders at a glance

## Front ends for your team and partners


### 1. Jet Admin


Jet Admin builds the front ends that run a business on top of an existing backend: admin panels, internal tools, dashboards and customer or partner portals. It connects to Postgres, MySQL, Supabase, Xano, Firebase, REST and GraphQL APIs and 200+ other sources, queries data in place and adds its own sign-in and roles, so each user sees only their rows. You describe the app and Jet generates it; custom React, Vue or Angular components and 2-way GitHub sync cover what the visual editor does not.


Users are unlimited on every plan. Granular permissions, SSO and audit logs are on the Business plan and above.


**Where it stops:** it is not for pixel-perfect consumer apps or marketing sites.


### 2. Softr


Softr builds portals and internal apps from blocks, fast, on Airtable and other sources.


**Where it stops:** when you need a component or logic its block library does not have.


### 3. Retool


Retool gives developers components and JavaScript to build internal tools on databases and APIs.


**Where it stops:** developer-first, with per-user pricing.


## Front ends for your customers


### 4. WeWeb


WeWeb is a visual front-end builder designed for external backends like Supabase and Xano, with full control over design.


**Where it stops:** internal admin screens take more work than in internal-tool builders.


### 5. Bubble


Bubble builds full web applications with workflows and a built-in database, and connects to APIs.


**Where it stops:** it works best when Bubble owns the data; external databases go through the API connector.


### 6. Glide


Glide builds mobile-first apps quickly on spreadsheets and SQL databases.


**Where it stops:** design flexibility and row limits by plan.


### 7. FlutterFlow


FlutterFlow builds native mobile and web apps in Flutter with Firebase, Supabase and API support.


**Where it stops:** mobile-first; back-office tools are not its focus.


### 8. Webflow


Webflow builds marketing sites with a visual editor and CMS.


**Where it stops:** it is a website builder, not an application front end.


## Which to use


- **Your team or partners need tools and portals on your backend:** Jet Admin.
- **You need a simple Airtable portal fast:** Softr.
- **Developers will build internal tools:** Retool.
- **You are building a customer-facing web app on Supabase or Xano:** WeWeb.
- **You want an all-in-one web app platform:** Bubble.
- **You need a mobile app:** Glide or FlutterFlow.
- **You need a marketing site:** Webflow.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is a no-code front-end builder?


A visual tool for building the interface of an app, screens, forms and navigation, on top of a backend you connect to.


### Can I use a no-code front end with my existing database?


Yes, if it has a native connector or can reach your API. Check whether it queries your data in place or copies it.


### Will I be locked in?


Your data stays in your backend. Lock-in is mainly in the front-end logic, which is why code export or GitHub sync matters.
